Purpose and how to read the order
The owner's signals and the hold flag
The order: every step with its trigger, flags, what stops and its proof
The order as a Mermaid graph
When each piece of the old line stops
Who builds the go-live tickets before and after the scheduler is live
Every wait of the sequence, its timeout and its fallback

pointers.shared: The seven unlanded steps this order places
Cancels, the PR 35 close, the design branch
The rulings that carry GOFACTORY, USERHALT and USERGO
Build mode, the flag the rebuild runs under

purpose.s: Every node ships dark and goes live by its own ticket with a named proof (dag.md section 7 rule 9); this volume is the order those tickets are cut and merged in, so no two volumes disagree about what goes first.

A step starts on its trigger record and ends on its proof record; nothing in the sequence starts by an agent typing, and a step that fails its proof three times is one card (principles.xml#three-attempts).

A flag goes live when its go-live ticket merges the flag's default in the service config and the service applies it by Reload on the merge record; the proof each step names is the node's own checklist item c-dark or its go-live text, cited by anchor.
Steps with the same number run in parallel; a later number waits for every proof of the earlier number it names in its trigger, and for nothing else.

signals.signal: The owner's halt (N-30 rule R01, or the Controls lever N-42) sets flag:hold. One stands today on the old line; step 0 records it into the new store as flag:hold set, so the new line starts held.
The owner's go for the rebuild (N-30 rule R03 or the GOFACTORY card). It starts the unlanded cleanup and the cut-over records and lets go-live tickets be cut; it does not clear flag:hold.

The owner's resume (N-30 rule R02 or the Controls signal lamp). It clears flag:hold, after which N-07 dispatches and N-09 merges. A USERGO before GOFACTORY is refused with a reply naming the hold (N-30 R02); a USERGO before step 7's proofs exist is accepted and the line simply has fewer live nodes, because each flag still gates its own node.
signals.s: flag:hold stops new dispatch (N-07) and new merges (N-09) only; ticks, health, backups, the poll, the push transport, the stable page, its watcher and its front door never stop (seat-contract.xml#halt-and-resume). The rebuild's own seats run under build mode, not under the line, so the hold does not stop them (memory build-mode-rule).

N-49 step 2 (the records cut-over, WO-20261012-99d6) needs flag:hold set by its own title; because the hold stands from step 0 until step 8 below, that wait finds it set; if the owner cleared it early, N-49's wait w2 applies (24 h, then one card).

step.does: The system comes up before anyone works: N-01 store, N-05 backups and N-06 unit, clock and health run as the user unit coq-service with every line flag false; N-43 loads the code table and the record kinds; the rulings C34 to C58 and the standing USERHALT become ruling records once, at bring-up, by coq owner import-answers over ~/.bearings/coq-stable/answers.jsonl and rulings-r02.jsonl (the import N-32's cut-over step 3 defines, run in the owner's one-time install under the owner's host CLI identity, shared/seat-contract.xml#relay; idempotent by card id), which sets flag:hold.
step.flags: none live; sched, gate, merge, verify, retry, stall, intake, inbox, push, cards, rail and phone_push all false
step.stops: Nothing yet. The legacy stable page (server.mjs and its wait.mjs loop) keeps serving the owner throughout; it is the always-on monitor until step 2.
step.proof: health:service SERVING, tick records for every subkind, a verified backup record, flag:hold set with the ruling id, and the ruling records for C34 to C58 (nodes/N-06/spec.xml#checklist, nodes/N-05/spec.xml#checklist).
step.dry-run: N-49 plans on every daily tick and its dry-run listing rides on the GOFACTORY card (nodes/N-49/spec.xml#mechanism step 1); nothing is applied.

step.does: N-50 writes the fourteen cancels and the PR 35 close (the design branch delete waits for the small-cut harvest, N-50 wait w3); N-49 runs its step 1 (back up first), then its steps 2 to 7 each on the previous step's success record (nodes/N-49/spec.xml#order); go-live tickets for steps 2 to 7 below are cut (see builders).
step.stops: The fourteen SPEC-16 tickets (cancel records); PR 35 (closed); the old line stays halted.
step.proof: fourteen cancel 200 records and pr.close 200 (nodes/N-50/spec.xml#checklist); disposition 200 for N-49 step 1.

step.does: The owner surface moves first, because the owner must see the new line before it moves: push.enabled (N-31), then intake.enabled (N-29) and inbox.enabled (N-30), then the watcher unit (N-27) and cards.enabled (N-28, which needs a live lamp), then rail.enabled (N-33); the page service runs dev and uat (N-32 cut-over steps 1 and 2) and the legacy state is imported once (N-32 cut-over step 3); then the one-shot unit coq-cutover@coq-stable swaps the stable page (N-32 cut-over step 4), which starts coq-watcher@coq-stable and coq-front-door@coq-stable and stops the legacy server and its wait loop.
step.flags: push, intake, inbox, cards, rail (in that order, each by its own ticket)
step.stops: wait.mjs and server.mjs on stable stop at cutover.swapped 201 (the script stops them itself, never a hand); front-door.mjs in the herdr pane stops when coq-front-door@coq-stable answers.
step.proof: cutover.swapped 201 with the stopped legacy pids, front-door 100 on the tailnet bind, watcher.alive alive for coq-stable, one card on stable produced from a test record within one tick (nodes/N-32/spec.xml#checklist, nodes/N-28/spec.xml#checklist).

step.does: CI as code: N-20 job.registered, N-21 namespace.ready, N-22 images pinned; N-23 to N-25 plan, run and post coq/gate on pull requests; the main protection requires coq/gate (the N-25 go-live proof); then gate.enabled (N-08).
step.stops: The webhook-driven gate path: line/bin/hook-listener.sh and line/config/hook.json handlers stop being started (N-04's poll is the correctness path, D06); their units are disposed of in step 4.
step.proof: protection.applied 200 naming coq/gate, a gate.verdict for the newest open pull request (nodes/N-08/spec.xml#runbook bring-up).

step.does: N-26 verifies the newest main sha in pods and writes main.gate.status; then verify.enabled (N-10); N-10 reads the legacy hold file once and owns the hold as a record from then on.
step.stops: At the first main.gate.status 201: line/bin/verify-main.sh is no longer called by anything and its hold file and worktrees are removed by N-45 (cleanup entries N-26 legacy-hold and legacy-verify-worktrees, nodes/N-26/spec.xml#runbook R3); the hook listener's units and handlers are removed by an N-49 step 7 disposition.
step.proof: a verified 201 for the newest merge whose main_sha equals origin/main (nodes/N-10/spec.xml#runbook bring-up) and the two cleanup.run 200 rows.

step.does: stall.enabled in shadow (judge and log, no revoke) for one day, then live (N-12); then retry.enabled (N-11).
step.stops: The idle alarm and the per-minute idle watches stay retired (rejected-with-reason.xml#idle-alarm).
step.proof: a stall no-progress record for a SIGSTOPped test run (nodes/N-12/spec.xml#runbook bring-up) and a failure record with handled_by set and its attempt record (nodes/N-11/spec.xml#runbook bring-up).

step.does: sched.enabled (N-07) while flag:hold is still set: the tick runs, dispatches nothing and counts the backlog, which proves the scheduler without moving the line; merge.enabled (N-09) the same way: every candidate is merge.held reason halt.
step.stops: factory/bin/route.sh, flow.sh, policy.sh and the five watch scripts are started by nothing once coq-service is enabled (nodes/N-06/spec.xml#start step 4); their units and cache copies are N-49 step 7 dispositions; this step's proof is that none ran for a day.
step.proof: sched:tick with leader true and held_by_hold equal to desired; merge.held records with reason halt; no route.sh process for a day in the N-51 line-ops audit.

step.trigger: N-49 step 2 done (the records cut-over merged)
step.does: The records live in the state root only; events/ and factory/state leave git (WO-20261012-99d6, run by the rebuild seats under the hold its title asks for).
step.stops: Every event.sh write into the repository tree.
step.proof: disposition 200 for N-49 step 2 and git status clean of events/ on main.

step.trigger: steps 2, 6 and 7 proofs, then the owner's USERGO ruling
step.does: The owner gives USERGO on the Controls screen or the page; N-29 clears flag:hold; N-07 dispatches from the next tick; N-09 merges on a green gate plus review.passed (D15).
step.stops: At the first merge record written by N-09: line/bin/merge.sh, merge-watch.sh and the tester, merger and verifier rows of factory/config/routes.json are retired by an N-49 step 7 disposition (rejected-with-reason.xml#tester-merger-verifier-seats).
step.proof: a dispatch record after the resume ruling, then a merge 200 and a verified 201 for the same ticket with no hand step in the N-51 audit.

step.trigger: inbox live on stable for one day (step 2 proof plus 24 h of ack ladders)
step.proof: one card on stable produces one push on the owner's phone within 10 s (nodes/N-52/spec.xml#start).

step.trigger: one day of the new stable page with zero page.down 500
step.does: The retire ticket removes make ask, make wait, reply.mjs, wait.mjs, server.mjs, front-door.mjs and the idle shutdown (N-32 cut-over step 5); cleanup-tier.sh --legacy removes ~/.bearings/coq-stable/ including wait.lock.json.
step.stops: The legacy page scripts, gone from the repository.
step.proof: the retire ticket's merge record and cleanup.run 200 for the legacy entry.

step.does: N-51 runs the exit test every day; the product freeze lifts on the first pass (D19).

diagram.mermaid: flowchart TD S0["0 system up, all flags false, flag:hold set from USERHALT"] --> G["GOFACTORY ruling"] G --> S1["1 N-50 cancels and PR 35 close; N-49 step 1 backups"] S1 --> S2["2 owner surface: push, intake, inbox, watcher, cards, rail; page swap stops wait.mjs and server.mjs"] S1 --> S3["3 CI as code; coq/gate required; gate on; hook listener not started"] S3 --> S4["4 main verify; verify on; verify-main.sh retired at first main.gate.status 201"] S4 --> S5["5 stall shadow then live; retry on"] S5 --> S6["6 sched and merge on under the hold; route.sh started by nothing"] S1 --> S7["7 N-49 step 2 records cut-over under the hold"] S2 --> U{"USERGO ruling"} S6 --> U S7 --> U U --> S8["8 hold cleared; first machine merge retires merge.sh and the old roles"] S2 --> S9["9 phone push after a day of acks"] S2 --> S10["10 retire legacy page scripts after a clean day"] S8 --> S11["11 exit test daily; freeze lifts on pass"]

legacy.s: route.sh (and flow.sh, policy.sh, the watch scripts): started by nothing once coq-service is enabled, step 6 proves a day without it, N-49 step 7 removes the units (#step-scheduler).
merge.sh and merge-watch.sh: retired at the first N-09 merge record after USERGO (#step-usergo).
verify-main.sh and its hold file: retired at the first main.gate.status 201 (#step-verify).
wait.mjs and server.mjs: stopped by coq-cutover@coq-stable at the page swap (#step-owner-surface), deleted by the retire ticket a clean day later (#step-retire-legacy-page).
hook-listener.sh and the hook.json handlers: not started from step 3, units removed at step 4 (#step-ci, #step-verify).
The fourteen SPEC-16 tickets and PR 35: step 1; the SPEC-16 design branch after the small-cut harvest (nodes/N-50/spec.xml#waits w3).

builders.s: Before step 6, nothing in the new line dispatches seats, so the go-live tickets of steps 2 to 6, N-49's land tickets and N-50's archive ticket are run by the rebuild plan's own seats under build mode scope rebuild (rebuild/factory-rebuild-plan.xml#steps; memory build-mode-rule), cut in this volume's order, one spec-author brief per step.

From step 8, every ticket request (nodes/N-03/spec.xml#input) becomes a spec-phase lease on a cut-request key and N-07 dispatches the spec-author (nodes/N-17/spec.xml#start); the rebuild seats stop taking new briefs.
Build mode expires by its own expiry (N-44); a rebuild ticket still open at expiry is one card, never a silent stop.

wait.timeout: none; the N-49 dry run refreshes daily on the card
wait.fallback: nothing runs; the card carries the newest listing (nodes/N-49/spec.xml#waits w1)

wait.timeout: P7D per go-live ticket (N-49 wait w3 shape)
wait.fallback: the ticket's N-11 dead path posts one card; later steps that do not name this step in their trigger proceed
go live on the day's record if no false stall was judged; one card naming the false stalls otherwise

wait.what: the owner's USERGO after steps 2, 6 and 7
wait.timeout: none; one card says the line is ready and names the proofs
wait.fallback: the card ages once to alert.aged at its escalation bound (status-codes.xml#escalation-bound); the line stays held and monitoring keeps running

wait.what: a day of the new stable page with zero page.down 500
wait.fallback: any page.down 500 restarts the 24 h window; three restarts is one card

many-agents.readers: Every spec-author, reviewer and the rebuild seats read this volume by step anchor; it holds no state, so any number read it at once.
many-agents.writers: One ticket at a time edits it (one file, one in-flight ticket); a node that changes its go-live proof edits its own volume and this step in one pull request.
many-agents.collision: Two go-live tickets of one step (push and intake) touch different nodes' config keys and never one file; two steps whose triggers race (step 2 and step 3 after step 1) are independent by construction; a go-live merged out of order is harmless because each flag gates only its own node and the hold gates the line, and the N-51 audit names the out-of-order flip.

source.note: the seven unlanded steps and the GOFACTORY trigger
D25 A: cleanup is the first slice after GOFACTORY
R-04 to R-10, the plan this order serves
nodes ship dark; the rebuild runs under build mode
the page and its wait never stop; USERHALT stops everything else
the system comes up before humans and agents
